messages:
jia: quick note — ran a small toy for a staggered/staged speculative decode (two-stage handoff: cheap sampler -> strong sampler if mismatch). curious if others think the eval is reasonable before I expand.
eli: drop the config pls
jia: config: cheap sampler = top-k(40) on quant4-ozma-13b @ 8-bit kernels, 1.0ms/token; strong sampler = beam(4)+top-p(0.95) on full fp16 model. handoff when cheap-sampler confidence < 0.6 (logprob gap heuristic).
sana: how are you measuring confidence? token-level gap or sequence score?
jia: token-level gap averaged over first 8 tokens, and a quick pass on prefix agreement < 0.7 triggers handoff. simple but fast.
matt: results?
jia: on a 5k prompt holdout (mix of short QA, longform, code), median latency p95 -> 28% reduction vs no-speculative (450ms -> 325ms). cost-ish: ~21% token compute saved.
katie: nice. quality regressions?
jia: end-to-end EM for QA tasks dropped 0.9% absolute. token-level exact-match on completion head dropped 1.8%. perplexity on heldout rose +0.6. not huge but nonzero.
eli: where's the regression concentrated? certain prompt types?
jia: mostly multi-step reasoning and code completions. short single-hop QA is fine.
sana: could be quant4 sampler introducing skew -> early handoffs on wrong candidates. did you try cheap sampler in fp16 to isolate quant effect?
jia: yes — cheap sampler in fp16 cuts the EM drop to 0.3% but latency savings drop to ~18%.
matt: that suggests quant noise on cheap sampler causes false negatives and unnecessary handoffs -> quality hit.
katie: any ablation on handoff threshold?
jia: tuned threshold from 0.5 to 0.75. at 0.7 we get sweet spot: 24% latency gain, EM -0.4%. 0.6 was where we originally saw -0.9%.
eli: what's the eval protocol? seed, sampling, metric definitions?
jia: 5k holdout drawn from production prompt buckets (QA 35%, longform 25%, code 20%, dialog 20%). fixed RNG for deterministic samplers, repeated each config 3x with different seeds for stochastic parts. metrics: p50/p95 latency, mean compute tokens, EM or exact-match where applicable, rouge-l for longform, top-1 token agreement, and generation PPL.
sana: good. add stratified breakdown by prompt length and category.
jia: noted.
matt: operationally, rolling this needs safe fallback. propose: default route = cheap sampler (quant4). if strong-sampler invoked, we send that request to dedicated fp16 pool but with a 300ms abandonment if not back -> fallback to cheap result and mark for async reevaluate.
katie: abandonment risky for correctness. better to let strong-sampler finish but mark as higher cost route then throttle.
eli: or hybrid: synchronous strong-sampler only for requests touching code/reasoning buckets; for short QA we accept cheap-only.
jia: agree — routing by bucket seems simplest.
ops-bot: deploy-check: can we shadow-route 1% traffic to compare? quick config: `speculative.staged.enabled = true`, `speculative.staged.threshold=0.7`, `speculative.staged.sample_pct=1`.
jia: I'll bake a canary plan: 1% shadow for 24h -> compare EM/ROUGE + latency at slice level. if EM drop <0.5% overall and no category drops >1.0% we proceed to 5%.
sana: also run a quant-isolation sweep: cheap sampler quant4 vs quant8 vs fp16 cheap to quantify noise.
jia: doing that next. early thought: maybe use small distillation of strong model for cheap sampler (same fp16 but lighter) to reduce mismatch.
matt: distillation might reduce mismatch but lose diversity. still worth prototype.
katie: action items?
jia: (1) run stratified ablation for thresholds 0.6/0.7/0.75 across quant4/quant8/fp16 cheap samplers (2) run 24h 1% shadow canary with routing-by-bucket (3) add logging for handoff reason and token-gap histogram (4) propose rollout playbook if canary meets quality SLOs.
eli: add cost calc for dedicated fp16 fallback too.
sana: I'll help on the metric dashboard. want p95 latency vs EM scatter and per-category deltas.
jia: thanks — will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
